text:
maya: Heads up — new 4-bit PTQ reranker (ranky3b-v2 -> int4-hybrid) shows ~3.2% NDCG@10 drop on bench-ranker-prodset-v2. Canary ran last night, small sample but consistent across tails. Any quick hypotheses?

devin: Oof. Is that vs fp16 or vs our int8 baseline?

maya: vs fp16. int8 looked fine (~0.4% drift). Larger hit on long queries (>200 tokens). NDCG@1 -5.1%, MRR -2.3% on the same holdout.

olga: Could be tokenization/preproc mismatch during quantization step — did you run PTQ on text after prod normalization? Any diff in tokenizer version or HTML stripping?

maya: Tokenizer is tkn-v3 (same as prod). But our eval harness applies whitespace-normalization for some cohorts; prod still has raw html in docs. Suspect doc formatting + trimming differences. I can pull a couple failing examples.

jordan: Also check candidate ordering — bench pipeline shuffles candidate pool pre-score, prod doesn't. That can amplify ndcg shifts if quantization affects top-1 logits.

maya: Good call. I'll re-run a small fixed-order holdout with exact prod preprocessing + no shuffle and compare fp16/int8/int4.

ci-bot: CI: rerank-eval/3932104321 queued by maya — tag=ranky3b-v2-int4-hybrid, dataset=bench-prodset-v2/prod-preproc, config="fixed-candidate-order". ETA ~25m

devin: Also add controls: fp16 baseline (same subset), int8 control, and record KV cache lengths. Int4 could be hitting kvpack edgecases on long contexts.

olga: If it's long-docs, try disabling prefix-caching and check prompt concat order (Q+D vs D+Q). Quant can change relative scale, so ordering might matter.

maya: Running 3 jobs now: 
- fp16 baseline (prod-preproc + fixed order)
- int8 PTQ (same)
- int4 PTQ (same) + prefix-cache disabled
I'll paste sample fail pairs once they finish.

ci-bot: CI: job 3932104321-1 finished — fp16 baseline: NDCG@10 = 0.432
ci-bot: CI: job 3932104321-2 finished — int8: NDCG@10 = 0.429 (-0.7% vs fp16)
ci-bot: CI: job 3932104321-3 finished — int4: NDCG@10 = 0.418 (-3.2% vs fp16)

jordan: Seems PTQ int4 is the culprit. Can we try per-channel quantization or layer-wise schemes? Also what calibration set was used — generic vs tail?

devin: Important: if calibration was generic, it might not capture tail doc token distribution. Use a tail-focused calset for PTQ. Also check for logit magnitude shifts; maybe apply a learned rescale (scaler) post-quant to recover ranking order.

olga: Quant often skews logits; try per-channel scales + small rescale (0.95–1.05) or a tiny temp adjust before softmax to see impact.

maya: Re-running int4 with per-channel scales + tail-calibration-set (n=5k) + rescale=0.98. Command i'm using: 

```bash
rerank-eval --model ranky3b-v2 --quant int4-perchannel --calset tail-cohort-5k \\n  --dataset bench-prodset-v2 --preproc prod-normalize --fix-order --no-prefix-cache \\n  --post-rescale 0.98
```

ci-bot: CI: job 3932104321-4 queued — int4-perchannel-tailcal+rescale0.98 (ETA ~30m)

devin: If that improves, propose adding a "quant-holdout" suite that includes tail cohorts and ordering parity to catch regressions earlier.

maya: Agreed. If per-channel still misses, fallback plan is: route long queries (>256 tokens) to int8 pool or fp16 until we have more stable int4 configs.

jordan: Ping me with 10 sample failures and i'll add tracing to see where logits collapse (layer, attention norm, or quant overflow).

ci-bot: CI: job 3932104321-4 finished — int4-perchannel-tailcal+rescale0.98: NDCG@10 = 0.426 (-1.4% vs fp16). Significant recovery.

maya: Nice — per-channel + tail calset + tiny rescale recovers ~1.8% NDCG. I'll open a PR to: (1) publish per-channel PTQ as default for ranking models, (2) add tail-calset to quant holdout, (3) add candidate-order parity test to bench.

devin: :thumbsup: sounds good. Can you also add a short eval note documenting exact cohorts and failure cases so we don't regress?

maya: Will do — will paste diffs + 10 failure pairs in this thread. Thanks team.
